clusters.headline: Indonesian Lawmakers Initiate Impeachment Process Against Gibran
aiSummaryBullets: DPR members are signing a formal proposal for the House's right to express an opinion regarding Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka.
The initiative follows a Supreme Court decision that invalidated the educational equivalency certificate held by the Vice President.

clusters.headline: Three Prominent PSI Leaders Resign To Focus On Government Roles
aiSummaryBullets: High-ranking members Giring Ganesha, Raja Juli Antoni, and Isyana Bagoes Oka have formally stepped down from the Indonesian Solidarity Party.
The officials cited the need to dedicate their full attention to their respective responsibilities within the government.

clusters.headline: Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka Faces Impeachment Calls
aiSummaryBullets: Calls for the resignation and impeachment of Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka are growing among political parties and public groups.
The movement follows judicial rulings from the Constitutional Court and Supreme Court regarding the vice president's educational documentation.

clusters.headline: Funeral Arrangements Announced For Senior Politician Panda Nababan
aiSummaryBullets: Panda Nababan, a prominent senior politician and journalist, passed away on November 9, 2026, due to leukemia.
His burial is scheduled for November 12, 2026, in Siborong-borong, North Tapanuli, North Sumatra, following traditional Batak funeral rites.

clusters.headline: Indonesian Disaster Agency Reviews Helicopter Safety After Crashes
aiSummaryBullets: Indonesia's National Disaster Management Agency (BNPB) is reviewing water bombing operational procedures following two helicopter crashes in Kalimantan.
The most recent incident in the Barito River resulted in the death of a crew member, whose body has been returned to Jakarta.

clusters.headline: Former National Police Chief Listyo Sigit Faces Ongoing Investigations
aiSummaryBullets: The Attorney General's Office is investigating potential connections between the former police chief and a nickel industry figure named Arif Kurniawan.
Reports indicate the National Police procured extensive surveillance technology valued at Rp36.1 trillion between 2018 and 2024.
